name: 10 Tauri
description: A naked-eye star 14.0 parsecs away, 1.6 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 22484: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.081 +/- 0.014 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.622 +/- 0.024

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 22484: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.139 +/- 0.016

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 22484: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5997 +/- 44

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 22484: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 71.6 +/- 0.54 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 14 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.6 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.081 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.622 solar radii and 5,997 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 22484: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
